One of the most annoying and unproductive aspects of Downvoting is the lack of accountability and context for why the post was downvoted. Far too often a post is downvoted because the voter disagreed with the post and not on whether the post was a valid argument or helpful to the discussion. Voat.co has a big edge on the competition by requiring an introduction period before being able to Downvote. My idea would further Voat.co's position as the most efficient and productive forum to express new and diverse ideas, without the inevitable bias that comes with an increasing number of users/voters.

By requiring a reply to each Downvote, each Downvote becomes a task for the voter. The voter must take the time to write something in the reply and this will therefore discourage frivolous Downvoting. A requirement of at least 2 words or more in the reply might help avoid gaming of this reply system.

Furthermore, with this system the OP can respond to the comments of the downvoter rather than be helpless to understand why the post was downvoted. OP can appropriately reasons and the other viewers can fairly weight he arguments.

I think it would be best for the Downvote replies to appear in the normal place below the OP but could be kept separate from the normally submitted replies, possibly with a +/- button to expand or collapse the Downvote replies. I think some Voaters would also enjoy an option in the main settings to block the view of Downvote replies.

BTW, I'm new to his subverse so sorry if this has been discussed before.
Require a Reply with every Downvote

Then you should require a reply with every upvote. Because you shouldn't have to explain yourself. Maybe you just didn't like the article they submitted because it was sad or something, (and you wanted to push the dislike button.)

The like button is an established way to approve a post based on agreement, high quality, whatever. Since this is a catch all vote there is no need to require a reply.

On the other hand the Downvote button is more appropriate for the users to be able to self select quality content, not based on whether they agree or not but rather if it contributes to the discussion. Downvoting to oblivion does not inspire open discussion but rather echo-chambers of groupthink.
